scenes.title: 1927 University of Berlin Workbench: Bluma Zeigarnik Sweeping a Two-Pieces-Left Jigsaw Into the Oak Drawer

layout.description: Sunlit tall-window 1927 Berlin oak workbench holding a completed folded-paper star set neatly to one side and a wooden jigsaw puzzle missing just two corner pieces right beside a deep sliding oak desk drawer.

positions.who: Bluma Zeigarnik (researcher in 1927 tailored cardigan, collared blouse, and pleated wool skirt)
positions.where: standing beside the oak workbench, reaching forward to sweep the 90%-finished wooden jigsaw tray into the open oak drawer
positions.facing: angled toward the seated adult volunteer across the workbench

positions.who: 45-year-old Berlin volunteer (in 1920s wool vest and rolled shirt sleeves)
positions.where: seated at the workbench with hand lifted holding the second-to-last wooden puzzle piece in mid-air as the tray slides out of sight
positions.facing: leaning forward toward the closing oak drawer

props.name: wooden jigsaw frame missing two pieces beside a finished folded-paper star
props.period_detail: 1927 Weimar tabletop craft puzzle in warm birch wood paired with a crisp finished paper star
props.physical_behavior: State-A open tabletop puzzle with two empty slots -> State-B swept briskly off the tabletop into the deep oak drawer before the volunteer's hand can drop the piece in

props.name: deep sliding oak desk drawer and cloth-bound 1927 recall ledger
props.period_detail: solid brass-pull Berlin laboratory drawer hiding all unfinished pieces out of sight
props.physical_behavior: State-A pulled open to swallow the unfinished puzzle -> State-B pushed shut with a crisp wooden click while Zeigarnik opens the recall ledger

actions.verb_sequence: sets the finished paper star aside without a second glance -> leans forward gripping the penultimate wooden jigsaw piece just above the slot
steps beside the table, sweeps the unfinished jigsaw tray into the oak drawer, pushes the drawer shut, and opens her ledger for immediate recall

reactions.reaction: keeps fingers poised in mid-air staring at the closed drawer and immediately names the unfinished puzzle first
logs the 1.9x unfinished-over-completed recall jump in her cloth notebook

scenes.wardrobe: 1927 Berlin academic attire: charcoal wool vest over crisp white shirt sleeves; olive knit cardigan over ivory blouse and midi wool skirt.
scenes.lighting: Bright natural morning daylight streaming through tall European casement windows.
scenes.recognition_hook: Finish a task and your brain drops it in seconds—sweep it into a drawer two pieces before the end and it dominates recall nearly two to one.

key_visual.description: a 1927 researcher at a sunlit oak workbench sweeping a nearly finished wooden jigsaw puzzle into a sliding desk drawer while a seated adult volunteer's hand reaches forward holding a puzzle piece

scenes.title: Outdoor 1926 Berlin Garden Cafe Terrace: The Waiter's Instant Memory Wipe 30 Seconds After Payment
scenes.era: 1926, outdoor sunlit sidewalk garden cafe, Berlin

layout.description: Open-air Berlin street-side garden terrace under chestnut trees with round marble bistro tables, porcelain coffee cups, and pastry plates.

positions.who: Veteran Berlin cafe waiter (in white waist apron, black vest, and bow tie)
positions.where: standing beside the outdoor bistro table snapping a leather billfold shut after taking cash
positions.facing: turning toward Kurt Lewin by the sidewalk hedge

positions.where: standing up beside the outdoor marble table, stepping back two paces to ask what was on the bill
positions.facing: facing the waiter on the sunlit terrace

props.name: leather cafe billfold and brass coin tray
props.period_detail: 1920s European outdoor bistro check folder and silver coffee service
props.physical_behavior: State-A held open while waiter recites six orders flawlessly -> State-B snapped shut over banknotes, triggering instant memory release

actions.verb_sequence: counts coins onto the brass tray, snaps the leather billfold shut, and tucks it into his apron -> lifts empty palms in blank surprise thirty seconds later

reactions.reaction: smiles in sudden realization and taps his pocket notebook to sketch the open-tab rule

scenes.wardrobe: 1920s outdoor cafe waistcoat and crisp white apron; tweed academic overcoat and round spectacles.
scenes.lighting: Crisp golden morning sunlight filtering through outdoor street trees.
scenes.recognition_hook: Two hours of complex unpaid orders held without paper—wiped clean thirty seconds after the bill is paid.

scenes.title: 5:30 PM Home-Office Shutdown Ritual: Closing the Open Loop With a Written Tomorrow Slot
scenes.era: Modern late-afternoon home study and outdoor front porch walk

layout.description: Warm modern home-office desk facing a sunlit neighborhood window, with an open laptop full of tabs beside a thick paper planner and fountain pen.

positions.where: sitting at the oak home desk writing a single concrete morning line in a paper planner before folding the laptop shut
positions.facing: angled toward the desk planner and sunlit window

props.name: hardcover daily planner and brushed-aluminum laptop lid
props.period_detail: contemporary adult home-office desk setup with warm brass desk lamp
props.physical_behavior: State-A glowing screen cluttered with open work tabs -> State-B pen writes next-morning time slot and hand folds laptop lid firmly shut

actions.verb_sequence: writes a two-line 9 AM plan into the paper notebook, caps the pen, and folds the laptop lid shut with one decisive hand

reactions.reaction: exhales deeply as tense shoulders drop into calm evening relief

scenes.wardrobe: Modern navy knit sweater over collared shirt.
scenes.lighting: Warm late-afternoon golden sunlight across oak desk.
scenes.recognition_hook: Hand your brain a concrete 9 AM appointment on paper, and it finally stops pinging you at 3 AM.
